        NotImplementedError: If ``psd_project=True`` gets a ``(T, M)``
            mask.

    Returns:
        A `FilterState` with the filtered and predicted means and
        covariances and the total log-likelihood.

    Examples:
        A random walk observed through its first component matches the
        sequential filter:

        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import gaussx
        >>> model = (jnp.eye(2), jnp.array([[1.0, 0.0]]), 0.1 * jnp.eye(2))
        >>> obs_noise = jnp.array([[0.5]])
        >>> observations = jnp.array([[0.1], [0.3], [0.2]])
        >>> prior = (jnp.zeros(2), jnp.eye(2))
        >>> state = gaussx.parallel_kalman_filter(
        ...     *model, obs_noise, observations, *prior
        ... )
        >>> state.filtered_means.shape, state.log_likelihood.shape
        ((3, 2), ())
        >>> sequential = gaussx.kalman_filter(*model, obs_noise, observations, *prior)
        >>> bool(jnp.allclose(state.log_likelihood, sequential.log_likelihood))
        True

        A masked step runs the predict only:

        >>> mask = jnp.array([True, False, True])
        >>> gated = gaussx.parallel_kalman_filter(
        ...     *model, obs_noise, observations, *prior, mask=mask
        ... )
        >>> bool(jnp.allclose(gated.filtered_means[1], gated.predicted_means[1]))
        True

        The square-root form agrees with the covariance form:

        >>> factored = gaussx.parallel_kalman_filter(
        ...     *model, obs_noise, observations, *prior, square_root=True
        ... )
        >>> bool(jnp.allclose(factored.filtered_covs, state.filtered_covs, atol=1e-5))
        True

    References:
        Särkkä, S. & García-Fernández, Á. F. (2021). Temporal parallelization
        of Bayesian smoothers. *IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control* 66(1),
        299-306.

        Yaghoobi, F., Corenflos, A., Hassan, S. & Särkkä, S. (2022). Parallel
        square-root statistical linear regression for inference in nonlinear
        state space models. arXiv:2207.00426.
    """
    if solver is not None and not woodbury_innovation:
        warn_deprecated(
            "parallel_kalman_filter(solver=...) has no effect unless "
            "woodbury_innovation=True: the associative-scan combinators use "
            "dense solves. Passing it otherwise is deprecated and will raise "
            "in gaussx 0.7.0."
        )
    if form == "sqrt":
        warn_deprecated(
            'form="sqrt" is deprecated: it is a PSD projection of the '
            "covariance-form combinator, not a square-root filter. Pass "
            'psd_project=True instead; form="sqrt" will be removed in gaussx 0.7.0.'
        )
        psd_project = True
    elif form != "covariance":
        raise ValueError("form must be 'covariance' or 'sqrt'.")
    if square_root:
        if psd_project or woodbury_innovation:
            raise ValueError(
                "square_root=True cannot be combined with psd_project=True "
                "(or form='sqrt') or woodbury_innovation=True."
            )
        return parallel_kalman_filter_factor(
            transition,
            obs_model,
            process_noise,
            obs_noise,
            observations,
            init_mean,
            init_cov,
            mask=mask,
        )
    if psd_project:
        # lazy import, cycle: _ssm._parallel_kalman_sqrt -> _ssm._parallel_kalman
        from gaussx._ssm._parallel_kalman_sqrt import parallel_kalman_filter_sqrt

        return parallel_kalman_filter_sqrt(
            transition,
            obs_model,
            process_noise,
            obs_noise,
            observations,
            init_mean,
            init_cov,
            mask=mask,
            solver=solver,
        )

    if woodbury_innovation:
        return kalman_filter(
            transition,
            obs_model,
            process_noise,
            obs_noise,
            observations,
            init_mean,
            init_cov,
            mask=mask,
            solver=solver,
            woodbury_innovation=True,
        )

    obs_size = observations.shape[-1]
    num_steps = observations.shape[0]

    # Empty observation window: match kalman_filter's empty-scan output.
    if num_steps == 0:
        return _empty_filter_state(init_mean, init_cov)

    transitions, obs_operators, process_noises, obs_noises, masks, _ = (
        _normalise_tv_inputs(
            transition,
            obs_model,
            process_noise,
            obs_noise,
            T=num_steps,
            mask=mask,
            M=obs_size,
        )
    )
    # Work per channel throughout: a (T,) gate is the special case where
    # every channel of a step shares one flag, so broadcasting it
    # reproduces the whole-step path exactly.
    if masks.ndim == 2:
        channel_masks = masks
    else:
        channel_masks = repeat(masks, "t -> t obs", obs=obs_size)
    step_active = reduce(channel_masks, "t obs -> t", "any")

    elements = _filter_elements(
        transitions,
        obs_operators,
        process_noises,
        obs_noises,
        observations,
        channel_masks,
        step_active,
        init_mean,
        init_cov,
    )
    # (F_cond,1:t, μ_x,t|t, Σ_x,t|t, Λμ_lik,1:t, Λ_lik,1:t) for every t
    _, filtered_means, scanned_covs, _, _ = jax.lax.associative_scan(
        _filter_combine, elements
    )
    filtered_covs = jax.vmap(symmetrize)(scanned_covs)

    predicted_means, predicted_covs = _predicted_moments(
        filtered_means,
        filtered_covs,
        transitions,
        process_noises,
        init_mean,
        init_cov,
    )

    log_likelihood_step = functools.partial(_log_likelihood_step, obs_size=obs_size)
    log_likelihood_steps = jax.vmap(log_likelihood_step)(
        observations,
        predicted_means,
        predicted_covs,
        obs_operators,
        obs_noises,
        channel_masks,
        step_active,
    )
    # log p(y_1:T) = ∑_t log p(y_t ∣ y_1:t−1)
    log_likelihood = jnp.sum(log_likelihood_steps)

    return FilterState(
        filtered_means=filtered_means,
        filtered_covs=filtered_covs,
        predicted_means=predicted_means,
        predicted_covs=predicted_covs,
        log_likelihood=log_likelihood,
    )

docs.title: parallel_rts_smoother(filter_state: FilterState, transition: Float[Array, '*T N N'] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator, process_noise: Float[Array, '*T N N'] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator | None = None, *, solver: AbstractSolverStrategy | None = None, form: str = 'covariance', psd_project: bool = False) -> tuple[Float[Array, 'T N'], Float[Array, 'T N N']]
docs.text:
Parallel RTS smoother via reverse jax.lax.associative_scan.

μ_x,t|T = μ_x,t|t + G_smooth,t (μ_x,t+1|T − μ_x,t+1|t)
Σ_x,t|T = Σ_x,t|t + G_smooth,t (Σ_x,t+1|T − Σ_x,t+1|t) G_smooth,tᵀ

with G_smooth,t = Σ_x,t|t F_t+1ᵀ Σ_x,t+1|t⁻¹. Pairs with parallel_kalman_filter and matches gaussx.rts_smoother to round-off, with O(log T) parallel depth.

Algorithm
  1. Build one smoothing element (G_smooth,t, μ_back,t, Σ_back,t) per step t < T, and (0, μ_x,T|T, Σ_x,T|T) for the last; the module docstring defines them.
  2. Run the reverse associative scan; μ_back,t and Σ_back,t of the result are μ_x,t|T and Σ_x,t|T.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default filter_state FilterState

Accepted for API symmetry; not threaded through.

None form str

'covariance' psd_project bool

If form is not "covariance" or "sqrt", or transition is neither a matrix nor a stack.

TypeError

Returns:

Type Description Float[Array, 'T N']

Tuple (smoothed_means, smoothed_covs) holding μ_x,t|T and

Σ_x,t|T.

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> import gaussx
>>> transition = jnp.eye(2)
>>> model = (transition, jnp.array([[1.0, 0.0]]), 0.1 * jnp.eye(2))
>>> observations = jnp.array([[0.1], [0.3], [0.2]])
>>> state = gaussx.parallel_kalman_filter(
...     *model, jnp.array([[0.5]]), observations, jnp.zeros(2), jnp.eye(2)
... )
>>> means, covs = gaussx.parallel_rts_smoother(state, transition)
>>> means.shape, covs.shape

>>> sequential_means, _ = gaussx.rts_smoother(state, transition)

def parallel_rts_smoother(
    filter_state: FilterState,
    transition: Float[Array, "*T N N"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    process_noise: Float[Array, "*T N N"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator | None = None,
    *,
    solver: AbstractSolverStrategy | None = None,
    form: str = "covariance",
    psd_project: bool = False,
) -> tuple[Float[Array, "T N"], Float[Array, "T N N"]]:
    """Parallel RTS smoother via reverse `jax.lax.associative_scan`.

        μ_x,t|T = μ_x,t|t + G_smooth,t (μ_x,t+1|T − μ_x,t+1|t)
        Σ_x,t|T = Σ_x,t|t + G_smooth,t (Σ_x,t+1|T − Σ_x,t+1|t) G_smooth,tᵀ

    with G_smooth,t = Σ_x,t|t F_t+1ᵀ Σ_x,t+1|t⁻¹. Pairs with
    `parallel_kalman_filter` and matches `gaussx.rts_smoother` to round-off,
    with ``O(log T)`` parallel depth.

    Algorithm:
        1. Build one smoothing element (G_smooth,t, μ_back,t, Σ_back,t) per
           step t < T, and (0, μ_x,T|T, Σ_x,T|T) for the last; the module
           docstring defines them.
        2. Run the reverse associative scan; μ_back,t and Σ_back,t of the
           result are μ_x,t|T and Σ_x,t|T.

    Args:
        filter_state: Output of `parallel_kalman_filter` or
            `gaussx.kalman_filter`.
        transition: Linear dynamics F_t, as a matrix, a stack over time or
            an operator; the same one passed to the filter.
        process_noise: Deprecated and ignored, as in `gaussx.rts_smoother`;
            it will be removed in gaussx 0.7.0.
        solver: Accepted for API symmetry; not threaded through.
        form: ``"covariance"``. ``"sqrt"`` is a deprecated spelling of
            ``psd_project=True``, removed in gaussx 0.7.0.
        psd_project: Build the smoothing elements from PSD-projected
            factors and combine the factors with QR, so the smoothed
            covariances are PSD. As in `parallel_kalman_filter`, the
            elements come from covariance-form quantities, so this is a
            PSD safety net rather than a square-root smoother.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``form`` is not ``"covariance"`` or ``"sqrt"``, or
            ``transition`` is neither a matrix nor a stack.
        TypeError: If an operator-typed ``transition`` has a time axis.

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(smoothed_means, smoothed_covs)`` holding μ_x,t|T and
        Σ_x,t|T.

    Examples:
        Smooth a filter run; it matches the sequential smoother:

        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import gaussx
        >>> transition = jnp.eye(2)
        >>> model = (transition, jnp.array([[1.0, 0.0]]), 0.1 * jnp.eye(2))
        >>> observations = jnp.array([[0.1], [0.3], [0.2]])
        >>> state = gaussx.parallel_kalman_filter(
        ...     *model, jnp.array([[0.5]]), observations, jnp.zeros(2), jnp.eye(2)
        ... )
        >>> means, covs = gaussx.parallel_rts_smoother(state, transition)
        >>> means.shape, covs.shape
        ((3, 2), (3, 2, 2))
        >>> sequential_means, _ = gaussx.rts_smoother(state, transition)
        >>> bool(jnp.allclose(means, sequential_means))
        True

        The last smoothed moments are the last filtered ones:

        >>> bool(jnp.allclose(means[-1], state.filtered_means[-1]))
        True
    """
    _warn_unused_process_noise("parallel_rts_smoother", process_noise)
    if form == "sqrt":
        warn_deprecated(
            'form="sqrt" is deprecated: it is a PSD projection of the '
            "covariance-form combinator, not a square-root filter. Pass "
            'psd_project=True instead; form="sqrt" will be removed in gaussx 0.7.0.'
        )
        psd_project = True
    elif form != "covariance":
        raise ValueError("form must be 'covariance' or 'sqrt'.")
    if psd_project:
        # lazy import, cycle: _ssm._parallel_kalman_sqrt -> _ssm._parallel_kalman
        from gaussx._ssm._parallel_kalman_sqrt import parallel_rts_smoother_sqrt

        return parallel_rts_smoother_sqrt(filter_state, transition, solver=solver)

    del solver

    filtered_means = filter_state.filtered_means
    filtered_covs = filter_state.filtered_covs
    num_steps = filtered_means.shape[0]
    state_size = filtered_means.shape[-1]

    if num_steps == 0:
        return (
            jnp.zeros((0, state_size), dtype=filtered_means.dtype),
            jnp.zeros((0, state_size, state_size), dtype=filtered_covs.dtype),
        )

    transitions = _transition_stack(transition, num_steps)
    inner_gains, inner_means, inner_covs = jax.vmap(_smoother_element)(
        filtered_means[:-1],
        filtered_covs[:-1],
        filter_state.predicted_means[1:],
        filter_state.predicted_covs[1:],
        transitions[1:],
    )
    # Last element: G_smooth,T = 0, μ_back,T = μ_x,T|T, Σ_back,T = Σ_x,T|T
    last_gain = jnp.zeros((1, state_size, state_size), dtype=filtered_means.dtype)
    smoother_gains = jnp.concatenate([inner_gains, last_gain])
    back_means = jnp.concatenate([inner_means, filtered_means[-1:]])
    back_covs = jnp.concatenate([inner_covs, filtered_covs[-1:]])

    # (G_smooth,t:T, μ_x,t|T, Σ_x,t|T) for every t
    _, smoothed_means, smoothed_covs = jax.lax.associative_scan(
        _smoother_combine, (smoother_gains, back_means, back_covs), reverse=True
    )
    smoothed_covs = jax.vmap(symmetrize)(smoothed_covs)
    return smoothed_means, smoothed_covs

docs.title: meanfield_kalman_filter(transition: Float[Array, '*T D D'] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator, obs_model: Float[Array, '*T M D'] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator, process_noise: Float[Array, '*T D D'] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator, obs_noise: Float[Array, '*T M M'] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator, observations: Float[Array, 'T M'], init_mean: Float[Array, ' D'], init_cov: Float[Array, 'D D'], *, block_size: int, mask: Bool[Array, ' T'] | Bool[Array, 'T M'] | None = None, solver: AbstractSolverStrategy | None = None, parallel: bool = False) -> FilterState
docs.text:
Mean-field Kalman filter over L = D_x / d independent state blocks.

log p(y_1:T) ≈ ∑_ℓ log p(y⁽ℓ⁾_1:T)

for the model of gaussx.kalman_filter with every input projected onto its diagonal blocks: F_t⁽ℓ⁾, H_t⁽ℓ⁾, Σ_η,t⁽ℓ⁾ and Σ_ε,t⁽ℓ⁾ for ℓ = 1, …, L. The L filters run under jax.vmap, O(T L d³) work instead of O(T L³ d³), at the cost of the posterior cross-block covariances. Dropping the off-block entries is the mean-field projection, exact when the true cross-block couplings are zero. The observation must split the same way: channel block ℓ, of length D_y / L, observes state block ℓ.

Accepts the time-invariant, time-varying and operator forms of gaussx.kalman_filter. A gaussx.BlockDiag whose sub-operators match the blocking is split without materialising the full matrix.

Algorithm
  1. Split F_t, H_t, Σ_η,t, Σ_ε,t, μ_x,0, Σ_x,0, y_1:T and the mask into their L diagonal blocks.
  2. Run gaussx.kalman_filter (or gaussx.parallel_kalman_filter) on every block under jax.vmap.
  3. Concatenate the block means, embed the block covariances in block-diagonal matrices and sum the block log-likelihoods.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default transition Float[Array, '*T D D'] | AbstractLinearOperator

Linear dynamics F_t, one for all steps, a stack over time or an operator.

required obs_model Float[Array, '*T M D'] | AbstractLinearOperator

Observation operator H_t, in the same forms; D_y must be divisible by L.

required process_noise Float[Array, '*T D D'] | AbstractLinearOperator

Model-error covariance Σ_η,t, in the same forms.

required obs_noise Float[Array, '*T M M'] | AbstractLinearOperator

Observation-error covariance Σ_ε,t, in the same forms.

required observations Float[Array, 'T M']

Observations y_1:T, one row per step.

required init_mean Float[Array, ' D']

Prior mean μ_x,0 of the initial state x₀.

required init_cov Float[Array, 'D D']

Prior covariance Σ_x,0 of x₀.

required block_size int

State block length d; D_x must be divisible by it.

required mask Bool[Array, ' T'] | Bool[Array, 'T M'] | None

Optional observation mask, as in gaussx.kalman_filter. A per-step mask gates whole steps for every block; a per-channel mask is split per block.

None solver AbstractSolverStrategy | None

Solver strategy for the per-block Σ_y,t. Sequential mode only; the parallel filter does not thread it through.

None parallel bool

When True, run each block through gaussx.parallel_kalman_filter (O(log T) depth on accelerators) instead of the sequential scan.

False

Returns:

Type Description FilterState

A gaussx.FilterState over the full state. Its covariances are

FilterState

block-diagonal embeddings of the block covariances, with exact

FilterState

zeros off-block.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If D_x is not divisible by block_size, or D_y is not divisible by the number of blocks L.

Examples:

Two independent random walks, each observed directly:

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> import gaussx
>>> model = (jnp.eye(2), jnp.eye(2), 0.1 * jnp.eye(2), 0.5 * jnp.eye(2))
>>> observations = jnp.array([[0.1, -0.2], [0.3, 0.0], [0.2, 0.1]])
>>> prior = (jnp.zeros(2), jnp.eye(2))
>>> state = gaussx.meanfield_kalman_filter(
...     *model, observations, *prior, block_size=1
... )
>>> state.filtered_covs.shape
(3, 2, 2)

With no cross-block coupling the full filter agrees:

>>> full = gaussx.kalman_filter(*model, observations, *prior)
>>> bool(jnp.allclose(state.log_likelihood, full.log_likelihood))
True

def meanfield_kalman_filter(
    transition: Float[Array, "*T D D"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    obs_model: Float[Array, "*T M D"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    process_noise: Float[Array, "*T D D"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    obs_noise: Float[Array, "*T M M"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    observations: Float[Array, "T M"],
    init_mean: Float[Array, " D"],
    init_cov: Float[Array, "D D"],
    *,
    block_size: int,
    mask: Bool[Array, " T"] | Bool[Array, "T M"] | None = None,
    solver: AbstractSolverStrategy | None = None,
    parallel: bool = False,
) -> FilterState:
    """Mean-field Kalman filter over L = D_x / d independent state blocks.

        log p(y_1:T) ≈ ∑_ℓ log p(y⁽ℓ⁾_1:T)

    for the model of `gaussx.kalman_filter` with every input projected onto
    its diagonal blocks: F_t⁽ℓ⁾, H_t⁽ℓ⁾, Σ_η,t⁽ℓ⁾ and Σ_ε,t⁽ℓ⁾ for
    ℓ = 1, …, L. The L filters run under `jax.vmap`, O(T L d³) work instead
    of O(T L³ d³), at the cost of the posterior cross-block covariances.
    Dropping the off-block entries is the mean-field projection, exact when
    the true cross-block couplings are zero. The observation must split the
    same way: channel block ℓ, of length D_y / L, observes state block ℓ.

    Accepts the time-invariant, time-varying and operator forms of
    `gaussx.kalman_filter`. A `gaussx.BlockDiag` whose sub-operators match
    the blocking is split without materialising the full matrix.

    Algorithm:
        1. Split F_t, H_t, Σ_η,t, Σ_ε,t, μ_x,0, Σ_x,0, y_1:T and the mask
           into their L diagonal blocks.
        2. Run `gaussx.kalman_filter` (or `gaussx.parallel_kalman_filter`)
           on every block under `jax.vmap`.
        3. Concatenate the block means, embed the block covariances in
           block-diagonal matrices and sum the block log-likelihoods.

    Args:
        transition: Linear dynamics F_t, one for all steps, a stack over
            time or an operator.
        obs_model: Observation operator H_t, in the same forms; D_y must be
            divisible by L.
        process_noise: Model-error covariance Σ_η,t, in the same forms.
        obs_noise: Observation-error covariance Σ_ε,t, in the same forms.
        observations: Observations y_1:T, one row per step.
        init_mean: Prior mean μ_x,0 of the initial state x₀.
        init_cov: Prior covariance Σ_x,0 of x₀.
        block_size: State block length d; D_x must be divisible by it.
        mask: Optional observation mask, as in `gaussx.kalman_filter`. A
            per-step mask gates whole steps for every block; a per-channel
            mask is split per block.
        solver: Solver strategy for the per-block Σ_y,t. Sequential mode
            only; the parallel filter does not thread it through.
        parallel: When ``True``, run each block through
            `gaussx.parallel_kalman_filter` (``O(log T)`` depth on
            accelerators) instead of the sequential scan.

    Returns:
        A `gaussx.FilterState` over the full state. Its covariances are
        block-diagonal embeddings of the block covariances, with exact
        zeros off-block.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If D_x is not divisible by ``block_size``, or D_y is not
            divisible by the number of blocks L.

    Examples:
        Two independent random walks, each observed directly:

        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import gaussx
        >>> model = (jnp.eye(2), jnp.eye(2), 0.1 * jnp.eye(2), 0.5 * jnp.eye(2))
        >>> observations = jnp.array([[0.1, -0.2], [0.3, 0.0], [0.2, 0.1]])
        >>> prior = (jnp.zeros(2), jnp.eye(2))
        >>> state = gaussx.meanfield_kalman_filter(
        ...     *model, observations, *prior, block_size=1
        ... )
        >>> state.filtered_covs.shape
        (3, 2, 2)

        With no cross-block coupling the full filter agrees:

        >>> full = gaussx.kalman_filter(*model, observations, *prior)
        >>> bool(jnp.allclose(state.log_likelihood, full.log_likelihood))
        True
    """
    state_size = init_mean.shape[0]
    obs_size = observations.shape[-1]
    if state_size % block_size != 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"State dimension {state_size} is not divisible by block_size {block_size}."
        )
    num_blocks = state_size // block_size
    if obs_size % num_blocks != 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Observation dimension {obs_size} is not divisible by the number "
            f"of blocks {num_blocks}."
        )
    block_obs_size = obs_size // num_blocks

    # F_t⁽ℓ⁾, H_t⁽ℓ⁾, Σ_η,t⁽ℓ⁾, Σ_ε,t⁽ℓ⁾
    transition_blocks = _split_diag_blocks(
        transition, num_blocks, block_size, block_size
    )
    obs_model_blocks = _split_diag_blocks(
        obs_model, num_blocks, block_obs_size, block_size
    )
    process_noise_blocks = _split_diag_blocks(
        process_noise, num_blocks, block_size, block_size
    )
    obs_noise_blocks = _split_diag_blocks(
        obs_noise, num_blocks, block_obs_size, block_obs_size
    )
    # y⁽ℓ⁾_1:T
    obs_blocks = rearrange(
        observations, "t (block obs) -> block t obs", block=num_blocks
    )
    # μ_x,0⁽ℓ⁾ and Σ_x,0⁽ℓ⁾
    init_mean_blocks = rearrange(
        init_mean, "(block state) -> block state", block=num_blocks
    )
    init_cov_blocks = _split_diag_blocks(init_cov, num_blocks, block_size, block_size)

    base_filter = parallel_kalman_filter if parallel else kalman_filter
    block_inputs = (
        transition_blocks,
        obs_model_blocks,
        process_noise_blocks,
        obs_noise_blocks,
        obs_blocks,
        init_mean_blocks,
        init_cov_blocks,
    )

    channel_mask = mask is not None and jnp.ndim(mask) == 2
    if channel_mask:
        mask_blocks = rearrange(mask, "t (block obs) -> block t obs", block=num_blocks)

        def _run_masked(*inputs):
            *model_inputs, mask_block = inputs
            return base_filter(*model_inputs, mask=mask_block, solver=solver)

        block_states = jax.vmap(_run_masked)(*block_inputs, mask_blocks)
    else:

        def _run(*inputs):
            return base_filter(*inputs, mask=mask, solver=solver)

        block_states = jax.vmap(_run)(*block_inputs)

    filtered_means = rearrange(
        block_states.filtered_means, "block t state -> t (block state)"
    )
    predicted_means = rearrange(
        block_states.predicted_means, "block t state -> t (block state)"
    )
    # log p(y_1:T) ≈ ∑_ℓ log p(y⁽ℓ⁾_1:T)
    log_likelihood = jnp.sum(block_states.log_likelihood)

    return FilterState(
        filtered_means=filtered_means,
        filtered_covs=_embed_block_diag(block_states.filtered_covs),
        predicted_means=predicted_means,
        predicted_covs=_embed_block_diag(block_states.predicted_covs),
        log_likelihood=log_likelihood,
    )

μ_x,t|T⁽ℓ⁾ = μ_x,t|t⁽ℓ⁾ + G_smooth,t⁽ℓ⁾ (μ_x,t+1|T⁽ℓ⁾ − μ_x,t+1|t⁽ℓ⁾)

  2. Run gaussx.rts_smoother (or gaussx.parallel_rts_smoother) on every block under jax.vmap.
  3. Concatenate the block means and embed the block covariances in block-diagonal matrices.

>>> observations = jnp.array([[0.1, -0.2], [0.3, 0.0], [0.2, 0.1]])
>>> state = gaussx.meanfield_kalman_filter(
...     *model, observations, jnp.zeros(2), jnp.eye(2), block_size=1
... )
>>> means, covs = gaussx.meanfield_rts_smoother(
...     state, jnp.eye(2), block_size=1

def meanfield_rts_smoother(
    filter_state: FilterState,
    transition: Float[Array, "*T D D"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    process_noise: Float[Array, "*T D D"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator | None = None,
    *,
    block_size: int,
    solver: AbstractSolverStrategy | None = None,
    parallel: bool = False,
) -> tuple[Float[Array, "T D"], Float[Array, "T D D"]]:
    """Mean-field RTS smoother over L = D_x / d independent state blocks.

        μ_x,t|T⁽ℓ⁾ = μ_x,t|t⁽ℓ⁾ + G_smooth,t⁽ℓ⁾ (μ_x,t+1|T⁽ℓ⁾ − μ_x,t+1|t⁽ℓ⁾)

    with one smoother gain G_smooth,t⁽ℓ⁾ per diagonal block ℓ. The backward
    pass paired with `meanfield_kalman_filter`: L independent
    `gaussx.rts_smoother` passes under `jax.vmap`. ``transition`` accepts
    the same forms as the filter and is projected onto its diagonal blocks.

    Algorithm:
        1. Split F_t and the filtered and predicted moments into their L
           diagonal blocks.
        2. Run `gaussx.rts_smoother` (or `gaussx.parallel_rts_smoother`) on
           every block under `jax.vmap`.
        3. Concatenate the block means and embed the block covariances in
           block-diagonal matrices.

    Args:
        filter_state: Output of `meanfield_kalman_filter`, or any
            `gaussx.FilterState` whose covariances are block-diagonal; the
            off-block entries are discarded.
        transition: Linear dynamics F_t, as in the filter.
        process_noise: Deprecated and ignored, as in `gaussx.rts_smoother`;
            it will be removed in gaussx 0.7.0.
        block_size: State block length d; D_x must be divisible by it.
        solver: Solver strategy for the per-block Σ_x,t+1|t. Sequential
            mode only.
        parallel: When ``True``, run each block through
            `gaussx.parallel_rts_smoother` instead of the sequential scan.

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(smoothed_means, smoothed_covs)`` holding μ_x,t|T and the
        block-diagonal Σ_x,t|T.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If D_x is not divisible by ``block_size``.

    Examples:
        Smooth a mean-field filter run of two independent random walks:

        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import gaussx
        >>> model = (jnp.eye(2), jnp.eye(2), 0.1 * jnp.eye(2), 0.5 * jnp.eye(2))
        >>> observations = jnp.array([[0.1, -0.2], [0.3, 0.0], [0.2, 0.1]])
        >>> state = gaussx.meanfield_kalman_filter(
        ...     *model, observations, jnp.zeros(2), jnp.eye(2), block_size=1
        ... )
        >>> means, covs = gaussx.meanfield_rts_smoother(
        ...     state, jnp.eye(2), block_size=1
        ... )
        >>> means.shape, covs.shape
        ((3, 2), (3, 2, 2))

        The off-block covariances stay exactly zero:

        >>> bool(jnp.all(covs[:, 0, 1] == 0.0))
        True
    """
    state_size = filter_state.filtered_means.shape[-1]
    if state_size % block_size != 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"State dimension {state_size} is not divisible by block_size {block_size}."
        )
    num_blocks = state_size // block_size

    _warn_unused_process_noise("meanfield_rts_smoother", process_noise)
    # F_t⁽ℓ⁾
    transition_blocks = _split_diag_blocks(
        transition, num_blocks, block_size, block_size
    )

    filtered_mean_blocks = rearrange(
        filter_state.filtered_means,
        "t (block state) -> block t state",
        block=num_blocks,
    )
    predicted_mean_blocks = rearrange(
        filter_state.predicted_means,
        "t (block state) -> block t state",
        block=num_blocks,
    )
    # The smoother never reads the log-likelihood; broadcast it so the
    # vmapped state has a block axis on every leaf.
    log_likelihood_blocks = jnp.broadcast_to(filter_state.log_likelihood, (num_blocks,))
    block_states = FilterState(
        filtered_means=filtered_mean_blocks,
        filtered_covs=_split_diag_blocks(
            filter_state.filtered_covs, num_blocks, block_size, block_size
        ),
        predicted_means=predicted_mean_blocks,
        predicted_covs=_split_diag_blocks(
            filter_state.predicted_covs, num_blocks, block_size, block_size
        ),
        log_likelihood=log_likelihood_blocks,
    )

    base_smoother = parallel_rts_smoother if parallel else rts_smoother

    def _run(block_state, transition_block):
        return base_smoother(block_state, transition_block, solver=solver)

    smoothed_mean_blocks, smoothed_cov_blocks = jax.vmap(_run)(
        block_states, transition_blocks
    )

    smoothed_means = rearrange(smoothed_mean_blocks, "block t state -> t (block state)")
    smoothed_covs = _embed_block_diag(smoothed_cov_blocks)
    return smoothed_means, smoothed_covs

docs.text:
Infinite-horizon Kalman filter with the fixed steady-state gain G_∞.

μ_x,t|t−1 = F μ_x,t−1|t−1
μ_x,t|t = μ_x,t|t−1 + G_∞ (y_t − H μ_x,t|t−1)

for the time-invariant model x_t = F x_t−1 + η_t, y_t = H x_t + ε_t with η_t ~ 𝒩(0, Σ_η) and ε_t ~ 𝒩(0, Σ_ε). The steady-state filtered covariance Σ_x,∞ solves the filtering DARE (gaussx.dare), and every step uses its predicted covariance Σ_pred,∞ = F Σ_x,∞ Fᵀ + Σ_η, its observation covariance Σ_y,∞ = H Σ_pred,∞ Hᵀ + Σ_ε and its gain G_∞ = Σ_pred,∞ Hᵀ Σ_y,∞⁻¹. No Riccati update runs per step, so a dense step costs O(D_x² + D_x D_y + D_y²) instead of O(D_x³).

Like the other filters it predicts first: init_mean is the mean μ_x,0 of x₀ and observations[0] is scored against F x₀. Because every step uses Σ_y,∞ and G_∞, the log-likelihood equals kalman_filter's only when that filter starts at the DARE fixed point (init_cov = dare(...).P_inf); from any other prior it approximates the transient. There is no init_cov argument for that reason, and no mask: a skipped update leaves the covariance off the steady state, which a fixed gain cannot follow. Use gaussx.kalman_filter for gappy data.

Every model argument accepts a dense array or a lineax.AbstractLinearOperator. Operator inputs keep their structural mv inside the scan; the sandwiches are materialised once outside it.

Algorithm
  1. Solve the DARE for Σ_x,∞ and G_∞, unless dare_result is given.
  2. Form Σ_pred,∞, Σ_y,∞ and log det Σ_y,∞ once, and the filtered covariance Σ_pred,∞ − G_∞ H Σ_pred,∞, which is Σ_x,∞ at the fixed point.
  3. Scan over t: predict μ_x,t|t−1 = F μ_x,t−1|t−1, form the residual r_t = y_t − H μ_x,t|t−1 and update μ_x,t|t = μ_x,t|t−1 + G_∞ r_t.
  4. Add log p(y_t ∣ y_1:t−1) = −½ (r_tᵀ Σ_y,∞⁻¹ r_t + log det Σ_y,∞ + D_y log 2π).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default transition Float[Array, 'N N'] | AbstractLinearOperator

Linear dynamics F.

required obs_model Float[Array, 'M N'] | AbstractLinearOperator

Observation operator H.

required process_noise Float[Array, 'N N'] | AbstractLinearOperator

required obs_noise Float[Array, 'M M'] | AbstractLinearOperator

required observations Float[Array, 'T M']

Observations y_1:T, one row per step.

required init_mean Float[Array, ' N'] | None

Prior mean μ_x,0 of the initial state x₀. Defaults to zeros.

None dare_result DAREResult | None

Precomputed gaussx.dare result holding Σ_x,∞ and G_∞. If None, the DARE is solved here. A result with converged=False raises an EquinoxRuntimeError (also under jit).

None max_iter int

Maximum DARE doubling steps, used only when dare_result is None.

100 tol float

DARE convergence tolerance, used only when dare_result is None.

1e-08 solver AbstractSolverStrategy | None

Solver strategy for Σ_y,∞; None uses structural dispatch.

None woodbury_innovation bool

When True, build Σ_y,∞ as a gaussx.LowRankUpdate on Σ_ε so a structured Σ_ε gets Woodbury solves and log-determinants.

>>> model = (0.9 * jnp.eye(2), jnp.array([[1.0, 0.0]]), 0.1 * jnp.eye(2))

def infinite_horizon_filter(
    transition: Float[Array, "N N"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    obs_model: Float[Array, "M N"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    process_noise: Float[Array, "N N"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    obs_noise: Float[Array, "M M"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    observations: Float[Array, "T M"],
    init_mean: Float[Array, " N"] | None = None,
    *,
    dare_result: DAREResult | None = None,
    max_iter: int = 100,
    tol: float = 1e-8,
    solver: AbstractSolverStrategy | None = None,
    woodbury_innovation: bool = False,
) -> FilterState:
    """Infinite-horizon Kalman filter with the fixed steady-state gain G_∞.

        μ_x,t|t−1 = F μ_x,t−1|t−1
        μ_x,t|t = μ_x,t|t−1 + G_∞ (y_t − H μ_x,t|t−1)

    for the time-invariant model x_t = F x_t−1 + η_t, y_t = H x_t + ε_t
    with η_t ~ 𝒩(0, Σ_η) and ε_t ~ 𝒩(0, Σ_ε). The steady-state filtered
    covariance Σ_x,∞ solves the filtering DARE (`gaussx.dare`), and every
    step uses its predicted covariance Σ_pred,∞ = F Σ_x,∞ Fᵀ + Σ_η, its
    observation covariance Σ_y,∞ = H Σ_pred,∞ Hᵀ + Σ_ε and its gain
    G_∞ = Σ_pred,∞ Hᵀ Σ_y,∞⁻¹. No Riccati update runs per step, so a dense
    step costs O(D_x² + D_x D_y + D_y²) instead of O(D_x³).

    Like the other filters it predicts first: ``init_mean`` is the mean
    μ_x,0 of x₀ and ``observations[0]`` is scored against F x₀. Because
    every step uses Σ_y,∞ and G_∞, the log-likelihood equals
    `kalman_filter`'s only when that filter starts at the DARE fixed point
    (``init_cov = dare(...).P_inf``); from any other prior it approximates
    the transient. There is no ``init_cov`` argument for that reason, and
    no ``mask``: a skipped update leaves the covariance off the steady
    state, which a fixed gain cannot follow. Use `gaussx.kalman_filter` for
    gappy data.

    Every model argument accepts a dense array or a
    `lineax.AbstractLinearOperator`. Operator inputs keep their structural
    ``mv`` inside the scan; the sandwiches are materialised once outside it.

    Algorithm:
        1. Solve the DARE for Σ_x,∞ and G_∞, unless ``dare_result`` is given.
        2. Form Σ_pred,∞, Σ_y,∞ and log det Σ_y,∞ once, and the filtered
           covariance Σ_pred,∞ − G_∞ H Σ_pred,∞, which is Σ_x,∞ at the
           fixed point.
        3. Scan over t: predict μ_x,t|t−1 = F μ_x,t−1|t−1, form the residual
           r_t = y_t − H μ_x,t|t−1 and update μ_x,t|t = μ_x,t|t−1 + G_∞ r_t.
        4. Add log p(y_t ∣ y_1:t−1)
           = −½ (r_tᵀ Σ_y,∞⁻¹ r_t + log det Σ_y,∞ + D_y log 2π).

    Args:
        transition: Linear dynamics F.
        obs_model: Observation operator H.
        process_noise: Model-error covariance Σ_η.
        obs_noise: Observation-error covariance Σ_ε.
        observations: Observations y_1:T, one row per step.
        init_mean: Prior mean μ_x,0 of the initial state x₀. Defaults to
            zeros.
        dare_result: Precomputed `gaussx.dare` result holding Σ_x,∞ and
            G_∞. If ``None``, the DARE is solved here. A result with
            ``converged=False`` raises an ``EquinoxRuntimeError`` (also
            under ``jit``).
        max_iter: Maximum DARE doubling steps, used only when
            ``dare_result`` is ``None``.
        tol: DARE convergence tolerance, used only when ``dare_result`` is
            ``None``.
        solver: Solver strategy for Σ_y,∞; ``None`` uses structural
            dispatch.
        woodbury_innovation: When ``True``, build Σ_y,∞ as a
            `gaussx.LowRankUpdate` on Σ_ε so a structured Σ_ε gets Woodbury
            solves and log-determinants.

    Returns:
        A `gaussx.FilterState` with the filtered and predicted means, the
        constant covariances Σ_pred,∞ − G_∞ H Σ_pred,∞ and Σ_pred,∞ broadcast
        over time, and the total log-likelihood.

    Raises:
        EquinoxRuntimeError: If the DARE did not converge.

    Examples:
        A damped random walk observed through its first component:

        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import gaussx
        >>> model = (0.9 * jnp.eye(2), jnp.array([[1.0, 0.0]]), 0.1 * jnp.eye(2))
        >>> obs_noise = jnp.array([[0.5]])
        >>> observations = jnp.array([[0.1], [0.3], [0.2]])
        >>> state = gaussx.infinite_horizon_filter(*model, obs_noise, observations)
        >>> state.filtered_means.shape, state.filtered_covs.shape
        ((3, 2), (3, 2, 2))

        Started at the DARE fixed point, `gaussx.kalman_filter` agrees:

        >>> steady = gaussx.dare(*model, obs_noise)
        >>> exact = gaussx.kalman_filter(
        ...     *model, obs_noise, observations, jnp.zeros(2), steady.P_inf
        ... )
        >>> bool(jnp.allclose(state.log_likelihood, exact.log_likelihood))
        True
    """
    if dare_result is None:
        dare_result = dare(
            transition,
            obs_model,
            process_noise,
            obs_noise,
            max_iter=max_iter,
            tol=tol,
            solver=solver,
            woodbury_innovation=woodbury_innovation,
        )

    transition_op = _as_operator(transition)
    obs_model_op = _as_operator(obs_model)
    process_noise_dense = _materialise(process_noise)
    # Keep Σ_ε lazy when the Woodbury path consumes the operator directly:
    # it avoids an O(D_y²) allocation for large structured noise (e.g. a
    # DiagonalLinearOperator with large D_y).
    if woodbury_innovation and isinstance(obs_noise, lx.AbstractLinearOperator):
        obs_noise_innov = obs_noise
    else:
        obs_noise_innov = _materialise(obs_noise)

    steady_covariance = _checked_steady_covariance(dare_result)
    steady_gain = dare_result.K_inf
    num_steps = observations.shape[0]
    obs_size = observations.shape[-1]
    state_size = transition_op.out_size()

    # --- steady-state moments, once ---
    # Σ_pred,∞ = F Σ_x,∞ Fᵀ + Σ_η
    steady_predicted_covariance = _steady_predicted_covariance(
        transition_op, steady_covariance, process_noise_dense
    )
    # Σ_y,∞ = H Σ_pred,∞ Hᵀ + Σ_ε
    steady_obs_covariance = _innovation_covariance(
        obs_model_op,
        steady_predicted_covariance,
        obs_noise_innov,
        woodbury=woodbury_innovation,
    )
    # log det Σ_y,∞
    steady_logdet = dispatch_logdet(steady_obs_covariance, solver)
    # H Σ_pred,∞
    obs_projection = _left_matmul(obs_model_op, steady_predicted_covariance)
    # G_∞ H Σ_pred,∞
    correction = einsum(steady_gain, obs_projection, "state obs, obs col -> state col")
    # Σ_pred,∞ − G_∞ H Σ_pred,∞, which is Σ_x,∞ at the fixed point
    steady_filtered_covariance = steady_predicted_covariance - correction

    def step(carry, obs_t):
        filtered_mean, log_likelihood = carry

        # μ_x,t|t−1 = F μ_x,t−1|t−1
        predicted_mean = _matvec(transition, filtered_mean)
        # H μ_x,t|t−1
        predicted_obs = _matvec(obs_model, predicted_mean)
        # r_t = y_t − H μ_x,t|t−1
        residual = obs_t - predicted_obs
        # μ_x,t|t = μ_x,t|t−1 + G_∞ r_t
        new_mean = predicted_mean + steady_gain @ residual

        # Σ_y,∞⁻¹ r_t
        whitened_residual = dispatch_solve(steady_obs_covariance, residual, solver)
        # r_tᵀ Σ_y,∞⁻¹ r_t
        mahalanobis = residual @ whitened_residual
        # log p(y_t ∣ y_1:t−1) = −½ (r_tᵀ Σ_y,∞⁻¹ r_t + log det Σ_y,∞
        #     + D_y log 2π)
        log_likelihood_step = -0.5 * (mahalanobis + steady_logdet + obs_size * _LOG_2PI)
        # log p(y_1:t) = log p(y_1:t−1) + log p(y_t ∣ y_1:t−1)
        new_log_likelihood = log_likelihood + log_likelihood_step

        new_carry = (new_mean, new_log_likelihood)
        return new_carry, (new_mean, predicted_mean)

    # The carry takes the model's dtype, not JAX's default float: a
    # default-float mean would meet the float32 Σ_y,∞ of a float32 model in
    # the solve above, which lineax rejects under x64.
    dtype = jnp.result_type(observations, steady_covariance, steady_gain)
    if init_mean is None:
        init_mean = jnp.zeros(state_size, dtype=dtype)
    init_mean = jnp.asarray(init_mean, dtype=dtype)
    zero_log_likelihood = jnp.zeros((), dtype=dtype)
    init_carry = (init_mean, zero_log_likelihood)
    final_carry, (filtered_means, predicted_means) = jax.lax.scan(
        step, init_carry, observations
    )

    filtered_covs = repeat(
        steady_filtered_covariance, "row col -> t row col", t=num_steps
    )
    predicted_covs = repeat(
        steady_predicted_covariance, "row col -> t row col", t=num_steps
    )

    return FilterState(
        filtered_means=filtered_means,
        filtered_covs=filtered_covs,
        predicted_means=predicted_means,
        predicted_covs=predicted_covs,
        log_likelihood=final_carry[1],
    )

def infinite_horizon_smoother(
    filter_state: FilterState,
    transition: Float[Array, "N N"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    process_noise: Float[Array, "N N"] | lx.AbstractLinearOperator | DAREResult,
    _legacy_process_noise: Float[Array, "N N"]
    | lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    | None = None,
    *,
    dare_result: DAREResult | None = None,
    solver: AbstractSolverStrategy | None = None,
) -> tuple[Float[Array, "T N"], Float[Array, "T N N"]]:
    """Infinite-horizon RTS smoother with the fixed steady-state gain G_smooth,∞.

        μ_x,t|T = μ_x,t|t + G_smooth,∞ (μ_x,t+1|T − μ_x,t+1|t)
        Σ_smooth,∞ = Σ_x,∞ + G_smooth,∞ (Σ_smooth,∞ − Σ_pred,∞) G_smooth,∞ᵀ

    with the steady-state smoother gain G_smooth,∞ = Σ_x,∞ Fᵀ Σ_pred,∞⁻¹,
    where Σ_x,∞ is the DARE's filtered covariance and
    Σ_pred,∞ = F Σ_x,∞ Fᵀ + Σ_η its predicted one. The smoothed covariance
    Σ_smooth,∞ is the same at every step and solves the discrete Lyapunov
    equation above.

    Algorithm:
        1. Form Σ_pred,∞ and solve for G_smooth,∞ against it.
        2. Solve Σ_smooth,∞ − G_smooth,∞ Σ_smooth,∞ G_smooth,∞ᵀ
           = Σ_x,∞ − G_smooth,∞ Σ_pred,∞ G_smooth,∞ᵀ for Σ_smooth,∞.
        3. Scan backwards from μ_x,T|T, correcting each filtered mean with
           G_smooth,∞.

    Args:
        filter_state: Output of `infinite_horizon_filter`.
        transition: Linear dynamics F.
        process_noise: Model-error covariance Σ_η. The positional prefix
            ``(filter_state, transition, process_noise)`` matches
            `gaussx.rts_smoother`.
        dare_result: The `gaussx.dare` result used in the filter, holding
            Σ_x,∞ (keyword-only). A result with ``converged=False`` raises
            an ``EquinoxRuntimeError``. The old positional order
            ``(filter_state, transition, dare_result, process_noise)`` still
            works with a ``DeprecationWarning`` until gaussx 0.7.0.
        solver: Solver strategy for Σ_pred,∞; ``None`` uses structural
            dispatch.

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(smoothed_means, smoothed_covs)`` holding μ_x,t|T and
        Σ_smooth,∞ broadcast over time.

    Raises:
        TypeError: If ``process_noise`` or ``dare_result`` is missing, or
            ``dare_result`` is passed positionally after ``process_noise``.
        EquinoxRuntimeError: If the DARE did not converge.

    Examples:
        Smooth an infinite-horizon filter run:

        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import gaussx
        >>> transition, process_noise = 0.9 * jnp.eye(2), 0.1 * jnp.eye(2)
        >>> model = (transition, jnp.array([[1.0, 0.0]]), process_noise)
        >>> obs_noise = jnp.array([[0.5]])
        >>> steady = gaussx.dare(*model, obs_noise)
        >>> observations = jnp.array([[0.1], [0.3], [0.2]])
        >>> state = gaussx.infinite_horizon_filter(
        ...     *model, obs_noise, observations, dare_result=steady
        ... )
        >>> means, covs = gaussx.infinite_horizon_smoother(
        ...     state, transition, process_noise, dare_result=steady
        ... )
        >>> means.shape, covs.shape
        ((3, 2), (3, 2, 2))

        Smoothing never inflates the variance:

        >>> bool(jnp.all(jnp.diag(covs[0]) <= jnp.diag(state.filtered_covs[0])))
        True
    """
    noise: Array | lx.AbstractLinearOperator | None
    if isinstance(process_noise, DAREResult):
        # Old order: (filter_state, transition, dare_result, process_noise).
        warn_deprecated(
            "infinite_horizon_smoother(filter_state, transition, dare_result, "
            "process_noise) is deprecated; pass process_noise third and "
            "dare_result as a keyword, as in rts_smoother. The old order will "
            "stop working in gaussx 0.7.0."
        )
        dare_result, noise = process_noise, _legacy_process_noise
    elif _legacy_process_noise is not None:
        msg = "infinite_horizon_smoother takes dare_result as a keyword argument."
        raise TypeError(msg)
    else:
        noise = process_noise
    if dare_result is None or noise is None:
        msg = "infinite_horizon_smoother requires process_noise and dare_result."
        raise TypeError(msg)

    transition_op = _as_operator(transition)
    process_noise_dense = _materialise(noise)
    steady_covariance = _checked_steady_covariance(dare_result)
    # Σ_pred,∞ = F Σ_x,∞ Fᵀ + Σ_η
    steady_predicted_covariance = _steady_predicted_covariance(
        transition_op, steady_covariance, process_noise_dense
    )

    steady_predicted_covariance_op = lx.MatrixLinearOperator(
        steady_predicted_covariance, lx.positive_semidefinite_tag
    )
    # Σ_x,∞ Fᵀ
    cross_covariance = _right_matmul_transpose(steady_covariance, transition_op)
    # G_smooth,∞ = Σ_x,∞ Fᵀ Σ_pred,∞⁻¹, row by row since Σ_pred,∞ is symmetric
    smoother_gain = solve_rows(
        steady_predicted_covariance_op, cross_covariance, solver=solver
    )

    # --- steady-state smoothed covariance ---
    # discrete_lyapunov_solve uses an eigendecomposition of G_smooth,∞
    # instead of materialising the (D_x², D_x²) Kronecker matrix
    # I − G_smooth,∞ ⊗ G_smooth,∞.
    # G_smooth,∞ Σ_pred,∞
    gain_covariance = einsum(
        smoother_gain,
        steady_predicted_covariance,
        "state next, next col -> state col",
    )
    # G_smooth,∞ Σ_pred,∞ G_smooth,∞ᵀ
    correction = einsum(
        gain_covariance, smoother_gain, "state col, other col -> state other"
    )
    # Σ_x,∞ − G_smooth,∞ Σ_pred,∞ G_smooth,∞ᵀ
    lyapunov_rhs = steady_covariance - correction
    # Σ_smooth,∞ − G_smooth,∞ Σ_smooth,∞ G_smooth,∞ᵀ
    #     = Σ_x,∞ − G_smooth,∞ Σ_pred,∞ G_smooth,∞ᵀ
    steady_smoothed_covariance = discrete_lyapunov_solve(smoother_gain, lyapunov_rhs)
    steady_smoothed_covariance = symmetrize(steady_smoothed_covariance)

    num_steps = filter_state.filtered_means.shape[0]

    def step(smoothed_mean_next, inputs):
        filtered_mean, predicted_mean_next = inputs
        # μ_x,t+1|T − μ_x,t+1|t
        mean_correction = smoothed_mean_next - predicted_mean_next
        # μ_x,t|T = μ_x,t|t + G_smooth,∞ (μ_x,t+1|T − μ_x,t+1|t)
        smoothed_mean = filtered_mean + smoother_gain @ mean_correction
        return smoothed_mean, smoothed_mean

    init_carry = filter_state.filtered_means[num_steps - 1]
    # Reverse the sequences for the backward pass (excluding the last step).
    inputs = (
        filter_state.filtered_means[:-1][::-1],
        filter_state.predicted_means[1:][::-1],
    )

    _, smoothed_means_rev = jax.lax.scan(step, init_carry, inputs)

    # Reverse back and append the last filtered mean.
    smoothed_means = jnp.concatenate(
        [smoothed_means_rev[::-1], filter_state.filtered_means[num_steps - 1 :]]
    )
    smoothed_covs = repeat(
        steady_smoothed_covariance, "row col -> t row col", t=num_steps
    )

    return smoothed_means, smoothed_covs

docs.text:
Steady-state Kalman filter covariance and gain (the filtering DARE).

Σ_pred,∞ = F Σ_x,∞ Fᵀ + Σ_η
Σ_y,∞ = H Σ_pred,∞ Hᵀ + Σ_ε,   G_∞ = Σ_pred,∞ Hᵀ Σ_y,∞⁻¹
Σ_x,∞ = Σ_pred,∞ − G_∞ H Σ_pred,∞

for the time-invariant model x_t = F x_t−1 + η_t, y_t = H x_t + ε_t with η_t ~ 𝒩(0, Σ_η) and ε_t ~ 𝒩(0, Σ_ε): the fixed point of the Kalman predict-update recursion. The predicted covariance solves the Riccati equation Σ_pred,∞ = Ric(Σ_pred,∞), with the Riccati map

Ric(Σ_pred) = F (Σ_pred − Σ_pred Hᵀ (H Σ_pred Hᵀ + Σ_ε)⁻¹ H Σ_pred) Fᵀ
            + Σ_η

which is solved with the structure-preserving doubling algorithm (SDA; Chu, Fan & Lin, 2005). SDA converges quadratically: after j doublings the error shrinks like the 2^j-th power of the closed-loop contraction rate, so slowly mixing dynamics (F near the unit circle) need a dozen or so doublings where iterating the recursion itself needs thousands (gh-294). Each doubling costs a few D_x × D_x solves.

Convergence is declared when the doubling iterate changes by at most tol relative to its largest entry; by quadratic convergence the returned solution is then accurate to about tol². Check converged when calling dare directly; infinite_horizon_filter and infinite_horizon_smoother raise on a non-converged result. A unique stabilising solution needs Σ_ε invertible and (F, H) stabilisable and detectable.

Gradients take the implicit path. The doubling algorithm is wrapped as an optimistix fixed-point solver for Ric and run through optimistix.fixed_point with optimistix.ImplicitAdjoint. The forward value is exactly the doubling solution; derivatives with respect to θ = (F, H, Σ_η, Σ_ε) follow from the implicit function theorem on g(Σ_pred, θ) = Ric(Σ_pred; θ) − Σ_pred,

∂Σ_pred,∞/∂θ = −(∂g/∂Σ_pred)⁻¹ ∂g/∂θ,

one linear solve at the fixed point instead of differentiating the iterations (Blondel et al., 2022). Without it jax.grad could not go through dare at all: reverse mode does not support the doubling while_loop. The solve materialises the D_x² × D_x² Jacobian of g and factors it densely (optimistix's default), so the backward pass costs O(D_x⁶): cheap for the state sizes of SDE kernels, heavy beyond D_x ≈ 50. The derivative is only meaningful when converged is True.

Algorithm
  1. Seed the doubling with Λ_obs^(0) = Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ H.
  2. Solve Σ_pred,∞ = Ric(Σ_pred,∞) by SDA, inside optimistix.fixed_point with the implicit adjoint.
  3. Form Σ_y,∞, solve for G_∞ and update to Σ_x,∞.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default A Float[Array, 'D D'] | AbstractLinearOperator

Linear dynamics F, as an array or an operator.

required H Float[Array, 'M D'] | AbstractLinearOperator

Observation operator H.

required Q Float[Array, 'D D'] | AbstractLinearOperator

Model-error covariance Σ_η.

required R Float[Array, 'M M'] | AbstractLinearOperator

Observation-error covariance Σ_ε.

required P_init Float[Array, 'D D'] | None

Deprecated and ignored: the doubling algorithm needs no initial guess.

None max_iter int

Maximum number of doubling steps.

100 tol float

Convergence tolerance on the relative change of the iterate.

1e-08 solver AbstractSolverStrategy | None

Solver strategy for Σ_ε and Σ_y,∞ (the seed and the final gain); None uses structural dispatch.

None woodbury_innovation bool

When True, build Σ_y = H Σ_pred Hᵀ + Σ_ε as a gaussx.LowRankUpdate, so a structured Σ_ε gets Woodbury solves.

False

Returns:

Type Description DAREResult

A DAREResult with the steady-state filtered covariance Σ_x,∞

DAREResult

(P_inf), the gain G_∞ (K_inf) and the convergence flag.

Examples:

A damped random walk observed through its first component:

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> import lineax as lx
>>> import gaussx
>>> transition = 0.9 * jnp.eye(2)
>>> obs_operator = jnp.array([[1.0, 0.0]])
>>> process_noise = 0.1 * jnp.eye(2)
>>> obs_noise = jnp.array([[0.5]])
>>> result = gaussx.dare(transition, obs_operator, process_noise, obs_noise)
>>> result.P_inf.shape, result.K_inf.shape, bool(result.converged)
((2, 2), (2, 1), True)

G_∞ is the Kalman gain of the steady predicted covariance:

>>> predicted = 0.81 * result.P_inf + process_noise
>>> gain = gaussx.kalman_gain(
...     lx.MatrixLinearOperator(predicted),
...     lx.MatrixLinearOperator(obs_operator),
...     lx.MatrixLinearOperator(obs_noise),
... )
>>> bool(jnp.allclose(gain, result.K_inf, atol=1e-4))
True

The Woodbury path with a diagonal Σ_ε gives the same fixed point:

>>> woodbury = gaussx.dare(
...     transition,
...     obs_operator,
...     process_noise,
...     lx.DiagonalLinearOperator(jnp.array([0.5])),
...     woodbury_innovation=True,
... )
>>> bool(jnp.allclose(woodbury.P_inf, result.P_inf, atol=1e-4))
True
References

Chu, E. K.-W., Fan, H.-Y. & Lin, W.-W. (2005). A structure-preserving doubling algorithm for continuous-time algebraic Riccati equations. Linear Algebra and its Applications 396, 55-80.

Blondel, M., Berthet, Q., Cuturi, M., Frostig, R., Hoyer, S., Llinares-López, F., Pedregosa, F. & Vert, J.-P. (2022). Efficient and modular implicit differentiation. NeurIPS 35.

    process_noise_dense = _materialise(Q)
    # Keep Σ_ε lazy when the Woodbury path consumes the operator directly:
    # it avoids an O(D_y²) allocation for large structured noise (e.g. a
    # ``DiagonalLinearOperator`` with large D_y).
    obs_noise_innovation = (
        R
        if woodbury_innovation and isinstance(R, lx.AbstractLinearOperator)
        else _materialise(R)
    )

    def _riccati(predicted_covariance, args):
        transition_d, obs_operator_o, process_noise_d, obs_noise_i, _ = args
        _, filtered_covariance = _filter_update(
            predicted_covariance,
            obs_operator_o,
            obs_noise_i,
            woodbury_innovation,
            solver,
        )
        # F Σ_x
        transition_covariance = einsum(
            transition_d, filtered_covariance, "next prev, prev col -> next col"
        )
        # F Σ_x Fᵀ
        propagated = einsum(
            transition_covariance, transition_d, "next col, other col -> next other"
        )
        # Ric(Σ_pred) = F Σ_x Fᵀ + Σ_η
        return symmetrize(propagated + process_noise_d)

    # Λ_obs^(0) = Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ H seeds the doubling iteration. It rides along in
    # ``args`` for the solver; the Riccati map ignores it, so the implicit
    # adjoint gives it a zero cotangent and H, Σ_ε are differentiated
    # through the map.
    dtype = jnp.result_type(transition_dense, obs_operator_dense, process_noise_dense)
    # Σ_ε⁻¹ H
    whitened_obs_operator = solve_matrix(
        _as_operator(R), obs_operator_dense, solver=solver
    )
    # Λ_obs^(0) = Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ H
    obs_information = symmetrize(
        einsum(
            obs_operator_dense,
            whitened_obs_operator,
            "obs row, obs col -> row col",
        )
    )
    process_noise_dense = process_noise_dense.astype(dtype)
    solution = optx.fixed_point(
        _riccati,
        _DoublingSolver(rtol=tol, max_iter=max_iter),
        jnp.zeros_like(process_noise_dense),
        args=(
            transition_dense.astype(dtype),
            obs_operator_op,
            process_noise_dense,
            obs_noise_innovation,
            obs_information,
        ),
        max_steps=None,
        adjoint=optx.ImplicitAdjoint(),
        throw=False,
    )
    steady_predicted_covariance = solution.value
    converged = solution.state.converged

    # G_∞ and Σ_x,∞ from the steady-state prediction Σ_pred,∞
    steady_gain, steady_covariance = _filter_update(
        steady_predicted_covariance,
        obs_operator_op,
        obs_noise_innovation,
        woodbury_innovation,
        solver,
    )

    return DAREResult(P_inf=steady_covariance, K_inf=steady_gain, converged=converged)

docs.text:
Joint Gaussian p(x_t, x_t+1) of each pair of consecutive states.

p(x_t, x_t+1) = 𝒩([μ_x,t; μ_x,t+1], [[Σ_x,t, Σ_x,t+1,tᵀ],
                                    [Σ_x,t+1,t, Σ_x,t+1]])

with the lag-one cross-covariance Σ_x,t+1,t = Cov[x_t+1, x_t] and t = 1, …, T − 1. The moments are usually smoothed ones, conditioned on y_1:T; the conditioning is left out of the symbols here.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default means Float[Array, 'T d']

Marginal means μ_x,t, one row per step.

required covariances Float[Array, 'T d d']

Marginal covariances Σ_x,t.

required cross_covariances Float[Array, 'Tm1 d d']

Lag-one cross-covariances Σ_x,t+1,t, one per consecutive pair.

required

Returns:

Type Description Float[Array, 'Tm1 two_d']

Tuple (joint_means, joint_covariances) holding the stacked mean

Float[Array, 'Tm1 two_d two_d']

[μ_x,t; μ_x,t+1] and the 2 × 2 block covariance of each pair, of

tuple[Float[Array, 'Tm1 two_d'], Float[Array, 'Tm1 two_d two_d']]

length 2 D_x.

Examples:

Three steps of a two-dimensional state give two pairs:

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> import gaussx
>>> means = jnp.zeros((3, 2))
>>> covariances = jnp.broadcast_to(jnp.eye(2), (3, 2, 2))
>>> cross = jnp.broadcast_to(jnp.array([[0.5, 0.1], [0.0, 0.5]]), (2, 2, 2))
>>> joint_means, joint_covs = gaussx.pairwise_marginals(
...     means, covariances, cross
... )
>>> joint_means.shape, joint_covs.shape
((2, 4), (2, 4, 4))

The diagonal blocks are the marginals and Σ_x,t+1,t sits below the diagonal:

>>> bool(jnp.allclose(joint_covs[0, :2, :2], covariances[0]))
True
>>> bool(jnp.allclose(joint_covs[0, 2:, :2], cross[0]))
True

def pairwise_marginals(
    means: Float[Array, "T d"],
    covariances: Float[Array, "T d d"],
    cross_covariances: Float[Array, "Tm1 d d"],
) -> tuple[Float[Array, "Tm1 two_d"], Float[Array, "Tm1 two_d two_d"]]:
    """Joint Gaussian p(x_t, x_t+1) of each pair of consecutive states.

        p(x_t, x_t+1) = 𝒩([μ_x,t; μ_x,t+1], [[Σ_x,t, Σ_x,t+1,tᵀ],
                                            [Σ_x,t+1,t, Σ_x,t+1]])

    with the lag-one cross-covariance Σ_x,t+1,t = Cov[x_t+1, x_t] and
    t = 1, …, T − 1. The moments are usually smoothed ones, conditioned on
    y_1:T; the conditioning is left out of the symbols here.

    Args:
        means: Marginal means μ_x,t, one row per step.
        covariances: Marginal covariances Σ_x,t.
        cross_covariances: Lag-one cross-covariances Σ_x,t+1,t, one per
            consecutive pair.

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(joint_means, joint_covariances)`` holding the stacked mean
        [μ_x,t; μ_x,t+1] and the 2 × 2 block covariance of each pair, of
        length 2 D_x.

    Examples:
        Three steps of a two-dimensional state give two pairs:

        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import gaussx
        >>> means = jnp.zeros((3, 2))
        >>> covariances = jnp.broadcast_to(jnp.eye(2), (3, 2, 2))
        >>> cross = jnp.broadcast_to(jnp.array([[0.5, 0.1], [0.0, 0.5]]), (2, 2, 2))
        >>> joint_means, joint_covs = gaussx.pairwise_marginals(
        ...     means, covariances, cross
        ... )
        >>> joint_means.shape, joint_covs.shape
        ((2, 4), (2, 4, 4))

        The diagonal blocks are the marginals and Σ_x,t+1,t sits below
        the diagonal:

        >>> bool(jnp.allclose(joint_covs[0, :2, :2], covariances[0]))
        True
        >>> bool(jnp.allclose(joint_covs[0, 2:, :2], cross[0]))
        True
    """

    def _single_pair(
        mean: Float[Array, " d"],
        mean_next: Float[Array, " d"],
        covariance: Float[Array, "d d"],
        covariance_next: Float[Array, "d d"],
        cross_covariance: Float[Array, "d d"],
    ) -> tuple[Float[Array, " two_d"], Float[Array, "two_d two_d"]]:
        # [μ_x,t; μ_x,t+1]
        joint_mean = jnp.concatenate([mean, mean_next])
        # Σ_x,t+1,tᵀ = Cov[x_t, x_t+1]
        cross_covariance_transpose = rearrange(
            cross_covariance, "next state -> state next"
        )
        # [[Σ_x,t, Σ_x,t+1,tᵀ], [Σ_x,t+1,t, Σ_x,t+1]]
        joint_covariance = jnp.block(
            [
                [covariance, cross_covariance_transpose],
                [cross_covariance, covariance_next],
            ]
        )
        return joint_mean, joint_covariance

    joint_means, joint_covariances = jax.vmap(_single_pair)(
        means[:-1],
        means[1:],
        covariances[:-1],
        covariances[1:],
        cross_covariances,
    )

    return joint_means, joint_covariances

docs.title: spingp_log_likelihood(prior_precision: BlockTriDiag, emission_model: Array, obs_noise: lx.AbstractLinearOperator, observations: Float[Array, 'N d_obs'], *, solver: AbstractSolverStrategy | None = None) -> Float[Array, '']
docs.text:
Log marginal likelihood log p(y_1:T) of a zero-mean SpInGP prior.

log p(y) = −½ (T D_y log 2π + T log det Σ_ε + ∑_t y_tᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y_t
               − (Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y)ᵀ Λ_x|y⁻¹ (Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y)
               + log det Λ_x|y − log det Λ_x)
Λ_x|y = Λ_x + blockdiag_t(H_tᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ H_t)

with T time steps and D_y observations per step. Every operation exploits the banded structure, for O(T D_x³) cost.

Algorithm
  1. Whiten H_t and y_t by one Cholesky factor of Σ_ε.
  2. Add the likelihood precision: Λ_x|y = Λ_x + H_tᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ H_t.
  3. Form the data term Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y and solve Λ_x|y against it.
  4. Take the banded log-determinants of Λ_x|y and Λ_x and assemble log p(y).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default prior_precision BlockTriDiag

Prior precision Λ_x of x_1:T, block-tridiagonal with T diagonal and T − 1 sub-diagonal D_x × D_x blocks.

required emission_model Array

Observation operator H_t, one for all steps or a stack over time.

required obs_noise AbstractLinearOperator

Observation-noise covariance Σ_ε, as an operator.

required observations Float[Array, 'N d_obs']

Observations y_1:T, one row per step.

required solver AbstractSolverStrategy | None

Solver strategy for the solve and log-determinant of Λ_x|y and Λ_x; None uses structural dispatch. Σ_ε always uses structural dispatch, since it is typically small.

None

Returns:

Type Description Float[Array, '']

The log marginal likelihood log p(y_1:T).

Examples:

A random-walk prior over three steps, observed directly:

>>> import jax.numpy as jnp
>>> import lineax as lx
>>> import gaussx
>>> prior = gaussx.BlockTriDiag(
...     jnp.array([[[2.0]], [[2.0]], [[1.0]]]),
...     jnp.array([[[-1.0]], [[-1.0]]]),
... )
>>> obs_noise = lx.MatrixLinearOperator(0.5 * jnp.eye(1))
>>> observations = jnp.array([[0.1], [0.3], [0.2]])
>>> log_likelihood = gaussx.spingp_log_likelihood(
...     prior, jnp.eye(1), obs_noise, observations
... )
>>> log_likelihood.shape
()

It equals the dense Gaussian density with Σ_y = Λ_x⁻¹ + Σ_ε:

>>> obs_covariance = jnp.linalg.inv(prior.as_matrix()) + 0.5 * jnp.eye(3)
>>> obs_covariance_op = lx.MatrixLinearOperator(
...     obs_covariance, lx.positive_semidefinite_tag
... )
>>> dense = gaussx.gaussian_log_prob(
...     jnp.zeros(3), obs_covariance_op, observations[:, 0]
... )
>>> bool(jnp.allclose(log_likelihood, dense, atol=1e-5))
True

def spingp_log_likelihood(
    prior_precision: BlockTriDiag,
    emission_model: Array,
    obs_noise: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    observations: Float[Array, "N d_obs"],
    *,
    solver: AbstractSolverStrategy | None = None,
) -> Float[Array, ""]:
    """Log marginal likelihood log p(y_1:T) of a zero-mean SpInGP prior.

        log p(y) = −½ (T D_y log 2π + T log det Σ_ε + ∑_t y_tᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y_t
                       − (Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y)ᵀ Λ_x|y⁻¹ (Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y)
                       + log det Λ_x|y − log det Λ_x)
        Λ_x|y = Λ_x + blockdiag_t(H_tᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ H_t)

    with T time steps and D_y observations per step. Every operation
    exploits the banded structure, for O(T D_x³) cost.

    Algorithm:
        1. Whiten H_t and y_t by one Cholesky factor of Σ_ε.
        2. Add the likelihood precision: Λ_x|y = Λ_x + H_tᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ H_t.
        3. Form the data term Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y and solve Λ_x|y against it.
        4. Take the banded log-determinants of Λ_x|y and Λ_x and assemble
           log p(y).

    Args:
        prior_precision: Prior precision Λ_x of x_1:T, block-tridiagonal
            with T diagonal and T − 1 sub-diagonal D_x × D_x blocks.
        emission_model: Observation operator H_t, one for all steps or a
            stack over time.
        obs_noise: Observation-noise covariance Σ_ε, as an operator.
        observations: Observations y_1:T, one row per step.
        solver: Solver strategy for the solve and log-determinant of
            Λ_x|y and Λ_x; ``None`` uses structural dispatch. Σ_ε always
            uses structural dispatch, since it is typically small.

    Returns:
        The log marginal likelihood log p(y_1:T).

    Examples:
        A random-walk prior over three steps, observed directly:

        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import lineax as lx
        >>> import gaussx
        >>> prior = gaussx.BlockTriDiag(
        ...     jnp.array([[[2.0]], [[2.0]], [[1.0]]]),
        ...     jnp.array([[[-1.0]], [[-1.0]]]),
        ... )
        >>> obs_noise = lx.MatrixLinearOperator(0.5 * jnp.eye(1))
        >>> observations = jnp.array([[0.1], [0.3], [0.2]])
        >>> log_likelihood = gaussx.spingp_log_likelihood(
        ...     prior, jnp.eye(1), obs_noise, observations
        ... )
        >>> log_likelihood.shape
        ()

        It equals the dense Gaussian density with Σ_y = Λ_x⁻¹ + Σ_ε:

        >>> obs_covariance = jnp.linalg.inv(prior.as_matrix()) + 0.5 * jnp.eye(3)
        >>> obs_covariance_op = lx.MatrixLinearOperator(
        ...     obs_covariance, lx.positive_semidefinite_tag
        ... )
        >>> dense = gaussx.gaussian_log_prob(
        ...     jnp.zeros(3), obs_covariance_op, observations[:, 0]
        ... )
        >>> bool(jnp.allclose(log_likelihood, dense, atol=1e-5))
        True
    """
    num_steps = prior_precision._num_blocks
    state_size = prior_precision._block_size
    # T D_y
    total_obs = observations.size
    # log 2π
    log_2pi = jnp.log(2.0 * jnp.pi)

    # --- posterior precision ---
    whitened = _whiten(emission_model, obs_noise, observations)
    # blockdiag_t(H_tᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ H_t)
    likelihood_precision = _build_likelihood_precision(whitened, num_steps, state_size)
    # Λ_x|y = Λ_x + blockdiag_t(H_tᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ H_t)
    posterior_precision = prior_precision.add(likelihood_precision)

    # --- quadratic terms ---
    # Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y
    data_vector = _build_data_vector(whitened)
    # Λ_x|y⁻¹ Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y
    posterior_solve = dispatch_solve(posterior_precision, data_vector, solver)
    # (Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y)ᵀ Λ_x|y⁻¹ Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y
    data_quadratic = jnp.dot(data_vector, posterior_solve)
    # ∑_t y_tᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y_t = ‖y_w‖₂²
    obs_quadratic = jnp.sum(whitened.whitened_obs**2)

    # --- log-determinants ---
    # log det Λ_x|y, large, so through the solver
    posterior_logdet = dispatch_logdet(posterior_precision, solver)
    # log det Λ_x
    prior_logdet = dispatch_logdet(prior_precision, solver)
    # T log det Σ_ε, from the same factor
    total_obs_noise_logdet = num_steps * whitened.obs_noise_logdet

    # log p(y) = −½ (T D_y log 2π + T log det Σ_ε + yᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y
    #     − (Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y)ᵀ Λ_x|y⁻¹ Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y + log det Λ_x|y − log det Λ_x)
    return -0.5 * (
        total_obs * log_2pi
        + total_obs_noise_logdet
        + obs_quadratic
        - data_quadratic
        + posterior_logdet
        - prior_logdet
    )

docs.title: spingp_posterior(prior_precision: BlockTriDiag, emission_model: Array, obs_noise: lx.AbstractLinearOperator, observations: Float[Array, 'N d_obs'], *, prior_mean: Float[Array, ' Nd'] | None = None, solver: AbstractSolverStrategy | None = None) -> tuple[Float[Array, ' Nd'], BlockTriDiag]
docs.text:
Posterior mean μ_x|y and precision Λ_x|y of x_1:T under SpInGP.

  4. Solve Λ_x|y μ_x|y against it.

>>> prior = gaussx.BlockTriDiag(
...     jnp.array([[[2.0]], [[2.0]], [[1.0]]]),

... )
>>> obs_noise = lx.MatrixLinearOperator(0.5 * jnp.eye(1))
>>> observations = jnp.array([[0.1], [0.3], [0.2]])
>>> mean, precision = gaussx.spingp_posterior(
...     prior, jnp.eye(1), obs_noise, observations
... )

The mean matches the dense Gaussian conditional:

>>> dense_precision = prior.as_matrix() + 2.0 * jnp.eye(3)

def spingp_posterior(
    prior_precision: BlockTriDiag,
    emission_model: Array,
    obs_noise: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    observations: Float[Array, "N d_obs"],
    *,
    prior_mean: Float[Array, " Nd"] | None = None,
    solver: AbstractSolverStrategy | None = None,
) -> tuple[Float[Array, " Nd"], BlockTriDiag]:
    """Posterior mean μ_x|y and precision Λ_x|y of x_1:T under SpInGP.

        Λ_x|y = Λ_x + blockdiag_t(H_tᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ H_t)
        μ_x|y = Λ_x|y⁻¹ (Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y + Λ_x μ_x)

    With ``prior_mean=None`` the prior is zero-mean and the Λ_x μ_x term
    vanishes.

    Algorithm:
        1. Whiten H_t and y_t by one Cholesky factor of Σ_ε.
        2. Add the likelihood precision: Λ_x|y = Λ_x + H_tᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ H_t.
        3. Form Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y, plus Λ_x μ_x when a prior mean is given.
        4. Solve Λ_x|y μ_x|y against it.

    Args:
        prior_precision: Prior precision Λ_x of x_1:T, block-tridiagonal.
        emission_model: Observation operator H_t, one for all steps or a
            stack over time.
        obs_noise: Observation-noise covariance Σ_ε, as an operator.
        observations: Observations y_1:T, one row per step.
        prior_mean: Prior mean μ_x of x_1:T, stacked to length T D_x (for
            example the ``mean`` half of
            `gaussx.MarkovGaussian.to_precision_form`); ``None`` means zero.
        solver: Solver strategy for the solve against Λ_x|y; ``None`` uses
            structural dispatch.

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(posterior_mean, posterior_precision)`` holding μ_x|y,
        stacked to length T D_x, and Λ_x|y as a `BlockTriDiag`.

    Examples:
        >>> import jax.numpy as jnp
        >>> import lineax as lx
        >>> import gaussx
        >>> prior = gaussx.BlockTriDiag(
        ...     jnp.array([[[2.0]], [[2.0]], [[1.0]]]),
        ...     jnp.array([[[-1.0]], [[-1.0]]]),
        ... )
        >>> obs_noise = lx.MatrixLinearOperator(0.5 * jnp.eye(1))
        >>> observations = jnp.array([[0.1], [0.3], [0.2]])
        >>> mean, precision = gaussx.spingp_posterior(
        ...     prior, jnp.eye(1), obs_noise, observations
        ... )
        >>> mean.shape, isinstance(precision, gaussx.BlockTriDiag)
        ((3,), True)

        The mean matches the dense Gaussian conditional:

        >>> dense_precision = prior.as_matrix() + 2.0 * jnp.eye(3)
        >>> dense = jnp.linalg.solve(dense_precision, 2.0 * observations[:, 0])
        >>> bool(jnp.allclose(mean, dense, atol=1e-5))
        True
    """
    num_steps = prior_precision._num_blocks
    state_size = prior_precision._block_size

    # --- posterior precision ---
    whitened = _whiten(emission_model, obs_noise, observations)
    # blockdiag_t(H_tᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ H_t)
    likelihood_precision = _build_likelihood_precision(whitened, num_steps, state_size)
    # Λ_x|y = Λ_x + blockdiag_t(H_tᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ H_t)
    posterior_precision = prior_precision.add(likelihood_precision)

    # --- posterior mean ---
    # Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y
    data_vector = _build_data_vector(whitened)
    if prior_mean is not None:
        # Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y + Λ_x μ_x
        data_vector = data_vector + prior_precision.mv(prior_mean)

    # μ_x|y = Λ_x|y⁻¹ (Hᵀ Σ_ε⁻¹ y + Λ_x μ_x)
    posterior_mean = dispatch_solve(posterior_precision, data_vector, solver)

    return posterior_mean, posterior_precision

docs.title: Precision-form chains
docs.text:
The joint prior or posterior of a Gauss-Markov chain has a block-tridiagonal precision \(\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_x\). The UDL factorisation \(\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_x = \mathbf{U} \mathbf{D} \mathbf{U}^\top\) — unit upper block-bidiagonal \(\mathbf{U}\), block-diagonal \(\mathbf{D}\) — is computed last block first by Schur complementation, for blocks \(t = 0, \ldots, T-1\) of size \(D_x\),

\[ \mathbf{D}_{T-1} = [\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_x]_{T-1,T-1} \] \[ \mathbf{U}_t^\top = \mathbf{D}_{t+1}^{-1} [\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_x]_{t+1,t} \] \[ \mathbf{D}_t = [\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_x]_{t,t} - [\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_x]_{t+1,t}^\top \mathbf{D}_{t+1}^{-1} [\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_x]_{t+1,t} \]

in \(O(T D_x^3)\). Unlike the banded Cholesky factor behind cholesky, its blocks have a physical reading: they are the state-space model with that precision, \(\mathbf{F}_t = -\mathbf{U}_t^\top\) and \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\eta,t}^{-1} = \mathbf{D}_t\) for \(t \ge 1\), with \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x,0}^{-1} = \mathbf{D}_0\). One pass therefore turns a precision-form posterior — the output of spingp_posterior, or a CVI / natural-gradient site update — into a chain that the Kalman machinery can sample, predict and interpolate from, without materialising the \((T D_x) \times (T D_x)\) covariance.

MarkovGaussian is the distribution that carries both views: its canonical parameterisation is the generative tuple \((\mathbf{F}_t, \mathbf{c}_t, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\eta,t}, \boldsymbol{\mu}_{x,0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{x,0})\), and to_precision_form / from_precision_form round-trip through the UDL factors exactly.

Structured linear algebra and Gaussian primitives for JAX.

Banded factorisation Λ_x = U D Uᵀ of a block-tridiagonal precision.

D_T−1 = [Λ_x]_T−1,T−1
U_tᵀ = D_t+1⁻¹ [Λ_x]_t+1,t
D_t = [Λ_x]_t,t − [Λ_x]_t+1,tᵀ D_t+1⁻¹ [Λ_x]_t+1,t

for blocks t = 0, …, T − 1 of size D_x. U is unit upper block-bidiagonal with super-diagonal blocks U_t, D = blockdiag(D_0, …, D_T−1), and [Λ_x]_t,t and [Λ_x]_t+1,t are the diagonal and sub-diagonal blocks of Λ_x; the recurrence runs backward through Schur complements.

This is not the Cholesky factor of Λ_x. For a Gauss-Markov chain x_t+1 = F_t x_t + η_t+1 with η_t+1 ~ 𝒩(0, Σ_η,t+1) and x₀ ~ 𝒩(μ_x,0, Σ_x,0), the blocks are exactly U_tᵀ = −F_t, D_t = Σ_η,t⁻¹ for t ≥ 1 and D_0 = Σ_x,0⁻¹, so one pass turns a precision-form posterior into a state-space model that can be sampled (see udl_to_ssm_params). Here F_t maps x_t to x_t+1, so it is the array A[t]; kalman_filter indexes the same matrix by the state it arrives at.

Every method costs O(T D_x³) (or O(T D_x²) for solve) and never forms the dense T D_x × T D_x matrix.

>>> precision = gaussx.BlockTriDiag(diag, sub)

>>> dense = precision.as_matrix()

>>> rebuilt = udl.as_block_tridiag().as_matrix()
>>> bool(jnp.allclose(rebuilt, dense, atol=1e-5))
